docs.title: Welcome to Chromaticity Help
docs.text:
This is the in-app help corpus shipped inside the Chromaticity desktop runtime. Pages here are authored clean-room from chromaticity's own ADRs and development standards — none of this content derives from any reference application's embedded documentation.

The Wave 1d-α PR 1 scaffold establishes the rails:

  • A mkdocs source tree under docs-corpus/docs/.
  • A static-HTML build emitted to dist/help/ and bundled into the Tauri binary via app/shell/tauri.conf.json bundle.resources.
  • A Help view (src/lib/views/Help.svelte) that surfaces the bundled HTML pages through Tauri's convertFileSrc resource path.

Future waves author the real corpus content: scene-format reference, operator hotkey catalog, MIDI / OSC routing, troubleshooting guides, and onboarding walkthroughs. The two pages shipped in PR 1 (this page and About) are placeholders that validate the routing + build pipeline end-to-end.

docs.title: About this Help corpus
docs.text: The Chromaticity Help corpus is a static documentation site built with MkDocs using the Material theme. The corpus is authored under docs-corpus/docs/ in the chromaticity source tree, built locally with mkdocs build, and emitted to dist/help/ for inclusion in the desktop application bundle.

docs.title: Authoring posture
docs.text: All Help corpus content is original chromaticity prose. Per the clean-room policy (docs/29-cleanroom-legal-policy-baseline.md), no text, structure, or per-page taxonomy is derived from any reference application's embedded documentation. Authors who land corpus content attest to clean-room provenance in the PR body.

docs.title: Build chain
docs.text:
The mkdocs build step runs locally before cargo tauri build so that the static HTML output exists at link time and is bundled into the desktop binary. CI does not currently run mkdocs build; that integration is Wave 1d-β release-eng scope.

This is the second placeholder page that exists to validate routing between corpus pages. Future waves replace this content with a real About / Version / Changelog page.

docs.title: Audio Reactivity
docs.text: Chromaticity is an audio-reactive runtime: every scene can sample tempo, energy, and per-band spectrum data from the live audio input and bind them as GLSL uniforms. This page describes how audio enters the engine, how the analysis pipeline produces uniform snapshots, and how the operator HUD widgets and the GLSL shader binding layer consume that data.

docs.title: Audio path overview
docs.text:
The audio pipeline runs across three thread boundaries, established by the runtime thread-and-process model:

  1. Audio input — Operating-system audio capture is owned by the audio analysis thread. A frame-source implementation pulls interleaved sample data, mixes multi-channel input down to mono, and produces a fixed-shape AudioFrame value type.
  2. Analysis — The same thread calls extract_uniform_snapshot on each frame. The function is pure: same input frame yields the same output snapshot. Its responsibilities are RMS, peak, an eight-band log-spaced FFT, and a single-frame autocorrelation BPM estimate.
  3. Hand-off — The producer-side runtime publishes the snapshot into a shared Arc<Mutex<AudioUniformSnapshot>> cell. The scheduler tick reads the cell, marshals it to GPU uniform inputs for the render path, and emits it to the UI over the engine-to-UI IPC bridge.

The audio crate intentionally does not depend on the render or IPC crates; consumers marshal the plain-data snapshot into whatever surface they own. This is what lets the analysis thread stay render-agnostic and lets the IPC bridge attach without any audio-side churn.

docs.title: What the snapshot carries
docs.text:
Each tick publishes the following fields:

Field Range Notes bpm [50, 220] Estimated tempo, clamped to the musical range; defaults to 120 on too-short frames rms [0, 1] Root-mean-square energy of the mono-mixed frame, clamped at 1 for out-of-range PCM input peak [0, 1] Peak absolute magnitude of the mono-mixed frame fft_bands[8] [0, 1] per band Eight log-spaced FFT magnitudes covering 20 Hz to 20 kHz

The snapshot is a #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)] value type; consumers can copy it freely without coordination. The default shape is the all-zero baseline that consumers see during the no-audio-yet startup window.

docs.title: The eight-to-four band reduction
docs.text:
The slice-1 producer publishes eight log-spaced FFT bands. Several operator-facing widgets expose four named bands ("bass", "low-mid", "mid", "high") to keep the UX legible. The reduction combines adjacent bands pairwise:

  • bass = (fft[0] + fft[1]) / 2
  • low-mid = (fft[2] + fft[3]) / 2
  • mid = (fft[4] + fft[5]) / 2
  • high = (fft[6] + fft[7]) / 2

This four-band view drives the AudioReactivity widget's named tile strip and the BPM strip below it. Authors who want raw eight-band resolution read chroma_AudioFFT directly in their GLSL.

docs.title: How the operator HUD uses live audio
docs.text:
Three visualizer widgets in the operator HUD read live audio over the IPC bridge:

  • AudioReactivity — Four named band tiles plus a tempo strip derived from bpm. The widget falls back to a synthetic time-domain function during the no-snapshot startup window so the UI is never blank.
  • BpmRing — Circular tempo indicator phase-locked to bpm. The ring's animation cadence reads the current snapshot directly; the synthetic fallback uses a fixed 120 BPM.
  • BeatDots — Discrete beat-pulse indicator that lights up on each beat boundary derived from bpm. The synthetic fallback fires at the same fixed tempo.

All three widgets implement a "live snapshot present" gate: when the last received snapshot is fresh, visuals run from real data; when the snapshot is stale or absent, the synthetic fallback paints. This dual mode is what lets the widgets ship as wireframe-faithful chrome before the live engine wiring lands and continue to work after the audio input source is silent.

The 48-bar FFT visualizer inside AudioReactivity and the inline 64-bar Spectrum surface in the Audio Uniforms view both stay synthetic-driven in the V1 release; live-driven retrofits are post-MVP UX work.

docs.title: Worked example: a radial pulse shader
docs.text:
A minimal scene that pulses on the bass band:

uniform float chroma_AudioFFT[8];
uniform float chroma_AudioRMS;
uniform vec2  iResolution;

void main() {
    vec2 uv  = (gl_FragCoord.xy - 0.5 * iResolution) / iResolution.y;
    float r  = length(uv);

    // Bass = bands 0 and 1 averaged.
    float bass  = 0.5 * (chroma_AudioFFT[0] + chroma_AudioFFT[1]);

    // Pulse: an inverse-distance ring that thickens with bass energy
    // and brightens with overall RMS.
    float pulse = smoothstep(0.40 - 0.20 * bass, 0.42, r)
                * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.42, 0.44 + 0.10 * bass, r));

    gl_FragColor = vec4(vec3(pulse * (0.5 + chroma_AudioRMS)), 1.0);
}

The same scene becomes a tempo-locked breathing pulse by mixing in syn_BPMSin against the radius. Authors can compose any of the audio uniforms; the binding adapter publishes them all in a stable per-pass order so per-pass uniform-buffer slot indices stay stable across reloads.

docs.title: Setting the audio threshold
docs.text:
The audio noise-floor gate is exposed as the syn_Threshold uniform and is operator-controllable through the audio settings panel and the OSC routes:

  • Shift+T samples the current 200 ms rolling RMS of syn_Level and sets the threshold to that value (also reachable as /audio/threshold/sample).
  • /audio/threshold {float} accepts an absolute threshold in [0, 1].

Audio hops with RMS below the threshold publish zeroed syn_Level* and syn_*Hits family uniforms. The threshold is the operator's primary tool for rejecting room noise, HVAC bleed, and crowd murmur in quiet sections of a show.

Authored from engine/audio/src/runtime.rs (producer thread shape), engine/audio/src/uniforms.rs (snapshot field semantics), engine/render/src/audio_adapter.rs (uniform binding contract), and the docs/adr/ADR-019-audio-uniform-ipc-bridge.md IPC contract combined with the docs/adr/ADR-006-thread-and-process-model.md thread-affinity invariants. Clean-room per docs/29-cleanroom-legal-policy-baseline.md.

docs.title: Chromaticity Uniform Reference
docs.text:
Chromaticity exposes two uniform namespaces to scene authors:

  • syn_* — the Synesthesia compatibility namespace (compat-syn-v1). These names exist for parity with reference scenes and are the primary surface authors should reach for when writing scenes that need to load on both runtimes.
  • chroma_* — the chromaticity-native namespace (native-chroma-v1). These names cover net-new analysis primitives and chromaticity-first surfaces that have no equivalent in the compatibility catalog.

Authors may mix the two namespaces freely inside a single scene. The binding adapter publishes the uniforms in a stable per-pass order; GLSL authors declare each uniform with its canonical name and type.

docs.title: Audio uniforms
docs.text: The audio analysis pipeline produces a per-tick AudioUniformSnapshot on the audio-analysis thread, which the audio-to-render adapter marshals into the GPU uniform slots below. The slice-1 producer is pure-data; the slice-2 BPM estimator carries a history-window median-smoother for tempo-following. Uniforms that read zero are the documented all-zero baseline for "no audio observed yet"; in production, the BPM uniform clamps to the default tempo (120 BPM) on the first tick before any analysis history accumulates.

docs.title: Scalar audio uniforms
docs.text: Uniform Type Range Description syn_BPM float [50, 220] Estimated tempo, clamped to the musical range syn_BPMConfidence float [0, 1] Tempo-stability confidence; near 1 when the estimator agrees across the history window syn_BPMTwitcher float [0, inf) Exponential "jump" clock; floor is the beat count, fract is the per-beat twitch syn_BPMSin float [0, 1] Sine wave at BPM frequency, beat-phase-locked syn_BPMSin2 float [0, 1] Sine wave at BPM divided by 2 syn_BPMSin4 float [0, 1] Sine wave at BPM divided by 4 syn_BPMTri float [0, 1] Triangle wave at BPM frequency syn_BPMTri2 float [0, 1] Triangle wave at BPM divided by 2 syn_BPMTri4 float [0, 1] Triangle wave at BPM divided by 4 syn_InputLevel float [0, inf) Pre-AGC instantaneous input level, computed as clamp(RMS / AGC_target, 0, inf) syn_RawLevel float [0, inf) Alias of syn_InputLevel with identical semantics syn_Threshold float [0, 1] Operator-settable noise-floor gate; audio hops below this value publish zeroed syn_Level* and syn_*Hits chroma_AudioRMS float [0, 1] Instantaneous root-mean-square energy of the mono-mixed audio frame chroma_AudioPeak float [0, 1] Instantaneous peak magnitude of the mono-mixed audio frame

docs.title: Array audio uniforms
Sampler audio uniforms
docs.text:
Uniform Type Channels Description syn_Spectrum sampler1D r=Raw FFT, g=Juiced, b=Smooth, a=Waveform Per-frame audio sampler with packed analysis variants syn_LevelTrail sampler1D r=Whole, g=Bass, b=Mid, a=High Per-band historical levels over time, newest sample at u=0

The eight-band split that chroma_AudioFFT[8] exposes is a separate surface from syn_Spectrum; the sampler retains parity with the compatibility catalog while the fixed-size array gives shader authors ergonomic indexing without a sampler lookup.

docs.title: Time uniforms
docs.text: Uniform Type Description syn_Time float Wallclock seconds since scene start syn_BassTime float Time accumulator that accelerates on bass-band hits syn_MidTime float Time accumulator that accelerates on mid-band hits syn_MidHighTime float Time accumulator that accelerates on mid-high-band hits syn_HighTime float Time accumulator that accelerates on high-band hits syn_CurvedTime float Same base as syn_Time with exponential acceleration on volume rises

docs.title: Authoring conventions
docs.text:
When a scene needs both raw analysis (the chroma_* audio primitives) and the smoothed / normalized parity surface (syn_Level*, syn_Spectrum), declare both uniforms; the binding adapter keeps the raw and smoothed paths independent so authors can pick the surface that matches each visual element. Avoid coining new syn_* names for chromaticity-native features — the Synesthesia namespace is reserved for compatibility coverage; net-new primitives belong under chroma_*.

The published GLSL spelling for every uniform on this page is exactly the canonical name; the runtime does not perform per-binding casing fixups. A typo at the GLSL declaration site silently leaves the uniform unbound, which surfaces as a warning at scene load and as a zero-valued sample at render time.

Authored from engine/render/src/audio_adapter.rs (canonical UNIFORM_NAME_* constants), engine/audio/src/uniforms.rs (producer shape and band semantics), docs/36-reactive-symbol-catalog.md (reactive symbol catalog), and the docs/adr/ADR-019-audio-uniform-ipc-bridge.md IPC contract. Clean-room per docs/29-cleanroom-legal-policy-baseline.md.

docs.title: Hotkey Reference
docs.text:
Chromaticity ships a fixed operator hotkey vocabulary covering scene and playlist transport, Snap-slot recall and capture, render and display control, the meta colour pipeline, audio threshold management, diagnostics, and show-state actions. Press ? at any time to toggle the in-app overlay that lists the same vocabulary against the active focus context.

The V1 hotkey map is read-only. Rebinding ships in V2 per the operator hotkey-map spec. The cap column on each row indicates whether the action is a free MVP capability or whether it requires an entitlement to fire; entitlement-gated rows fail closed when the matching capability is absent.

docs.title: Control-focused mode
docs.text:
Active only while a single control has keyboard focus. Esc exits control-focused mode.

Key Action D Set control to its default value R Set control to a random value in its range P Set control to its value in the current preset L Toggle the control's lock state (ignore randomization)

docs.title: Scene and playlist transport
docs.text: Key Action OSC cap Space Toggle playlist play/pause /playlist/toggleplay free ->, K Next scene in playlist /playlist/next free <-, J Previous scene in playlist /playlist/previous free Alt+Cmd+->, Ctrl+Alt+-> Jump to last in playlist /playlists/position -1 free Alt+Cmd+<-, Ctrl+Alt+<- Jump to first in playlist /playlists/position 0 free Enter Launch selected scene from the library /scenes/{name} free Shift+Enter Launch selected scene with preset prompt /scenes/{name} {preset} free Cmd+Enter, Ctrl+Enter Launch selected scene into a playlist slot (internal) free

docs.title: Snap slots
docs.text:
Per-scene quick-recall preset slots. The wire literal favslot is retained under compat-syn-v1 for OSC compatibility; the operator surface uses the name "Snap".

Key Action OSC cap 1 to 9, 0 Recall Snap slot 1 to 10 for the current scene /favslots/{n} (apply) free Shift+1 to Shift+0 Save current state to Snap slot 1 to 10 (overwrite without prompt) /favslots/{n}/save free Alt+Shift+1 to Alt+Shift+0 Clear Snap slot 1 to 10 (confirmation prompt) /favslots/{n}/clear free Cmd+S, Ctrl+S Save current state to the next empty Snap slot /favslots/{auto}/save free Cmd+Opt+S, Ctrl+Alt+S Save as a new named preset (prompts for name) /presets/new {name} free Cmd+0, Ctrl+0 Recall the scene's "gold" preset (Snap 0) /favslots/0 (apply) free

docs.title: Display and output
docs.text: Key Action cap F Toggle fullscreen on the primary output free Shift+F Toggle fullscreen on the secondary output (multi-display) free Cmd+Shift+F, Ctrl+Shift+F Cycle output window placement across displays free Cmd+\, Ctrl+\ Swap primary and secondary output free

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
Cmd+0 is globally bound to Snap 0; the former "reset resolution" binding has moved to Cmd+9.

Key Action OSC cap . Toggle render loop on/off /render/enabled {0|1} free , Toggle render-preview window (internal) free Cmd+=, Ctrl+= Step render resolution up /render/resolution {w} {h} render.custom-resolution Cmd+-, Ctrl+- Step render resolution down /render/resolution {w} {h} render.custom-resolution Cmd+9, Ctrl+9 Reset render resolution to scene default /render/resolution {sceneW} {sceneH} render.custom-resolution Cmd+Shift+=, Ctrl+Shift+= Open FPS target dialog /render/fps {float} free

docs.title: Meta controls
docs.text:
Each row enters a modal slider-adjust mode (arrow keys or scroll wheel). Esc exits the modal. The glsl column names the meta-colour uniform the binding maps onto.

Key Action glsl M Master _Master B Brightness _Brightness G Gamma _Gamma C Contrast _Contrast H Hue _Hue Y Saturation _Saturation I Invert toggle (no modal; binary flip) _Invert V Vertical mirror toggle _Vert_Mirror Shift+V Horizontal mirror toggle _Hor_Mirror E Dichrome toggle (from "Edition") _Limit_Colors

docs.title: Audio
docs.text: Key Action OSC cap A Toggle audio-input mute (internal) free Cmd+A, Ctrl+A Open audio settings panel (internal) free T Toggle audio-threshold visualizer overlay (internal) free Shift+T Set audio threshold to current RMS level /audio/threshold/sample free

docs.text: Key Action Cmd+K, Ctrl+K Open command palette (searches scenes, presets, settings, help) Cmd+/, Ctrl+/ Open help and docs search Cmd+L, Ctrl+L Open scene library Cmd+,, Ctrl+, Open settings Cmd+O, Ctrl+O Open OSC and MIDI mapping panel

docs.text:

docs.title: OSC Route Reference
docs.text: Chromaticity exposes Open Sound Control (OSC) inbound and outbound routes for show-control automation and external surface integration. This page enumerates the canonical route taxonomy honoured by the OSC adapter at the top-level prefixes the slice-2 route schema declares.

docs.title: Defaults and discovery
docs.text:
By default the OSC adapter binds the inbound listener to the loopback interface (127.0.0.1) and treats the outbound target as loopback until the operator configures a routable address. Exposing the inbound listener on a routable interface is an explicit operator opt-in. The operator can confirm the bound interface and current rate-limit posture through the AdapterPill chrome at the top of any view.

Two payload-hardening defaults are pinned by the network adapter:

  • The maximum accepted OSC packet size is 64 KiB. Oversize packets are rejected with an osc-malformed-class diagnostic and no state mutation.
  • The maximum nested OSC bundle depth is 4. Deeper payloads are rejected for the same reason.

Per-route inbound traffic is rate-limited at a default ceiling of 100 messages per second per (adapter, route) pair. Over-rate messages are dropped with an osc-rate-limited diagnostic emitted no more than once per second per route to prevent the diagnostics channel itself from saturating.

docs.title: Top-level prefixes
docs.text:
The slice-2 route schema declares four canonical top-level prefixes; addresses outside this set are rejected at parse time.

Prefix Purpose /controls Scene-author parameter control (control-bank reads and writes) /scenes Scene-selection and scene-launch routes /audio Audio-pipeline routes (threshold, level discovery) /render Render-loop and resolution control

Companion route families used by the operator hotkey vocabulary (/playlist, /playlists, /favslots, /presets) are part of the broader IO surface specified in the integrations document; see the plurality and alias rules below.

docs.title: Scene routes
docs.text:
Route Direction Args Description /scenes outbound (list payload) Library scene-name listing emitted on bind and on library-change /scenes/{name} {preset?} inbound scene name; optional preset name Launch scene; unsupplied preset resolves to Snap 0 / gold /scenes/{name} outbound scene name Scene-change announcement emitted on every cut or transition completion

The legacy singular-root forms /scene/{name} and /scene/{name} {preset} are accepted as compat-syn-v1 aliases. Outbound emission during the dual-emit window publishes both the canonical plural form and the singular alias.

docs.title: Snap (favslots) routes
docs.text:
Snap is the operator-facing name for per-scene quick-recall slots; the wire-level literal favslots is retained under compat-syn-v1 for compatibility.

Route Direction Args Description /favslots/{n} inbound (apply) slot index n in [0, 15] Recall Snap slot n for the current scene /favslots/{n}/save inbound (save) slot index n Overwrite Snap slot n with the current state /favslots/{n}/clear inbound (clear) slot index n Delete Snap slot n; the slot returns to unbound /favslots/{n}/name {string} outbound slot index, name string Snap-slot name announcement on show load and after any save or clear

The apply / save / clear distinction is wire-level explicit through the route suffix; there is no implicit mode selection from message arguments. The legacy /favslots/{n} {mode} form with a string argument of "apply", "save", or "clear" is accepted as a compat-syn-v1 alias.

docs.title: Playlist routes
docs.text:
Route Direction Args Description /playlists outbound (list payload) Show-playlist listing on bind /playlists/next inbound (none) Advance to next scene in playlist /playlists/previous inbound (none) Step back to previous scene in playlist /playlists/position {i} inbound integer index; negative counts from end Jump to absolute playlist position /playlists/play inbound (none) Resume playlist transport /playlists/toggleplay inbound (none) Toggle playlist play / pause /playlists/select {name} inbound playlist name Select a named playlist as the active one /playlists/current {name} outbound active playlist name Emitted on playlist change /playlists/position {i} outbound current position Emitted on every position change

The singular-root action forms /playlist/next, /playlist/previous, /playlist/toggleplay are accepted as compat-syn-v1 aliases for the plural-root canonical forms. The hotkey overlay surfaces these singular forms in its OSC column for compatibility with reference scenes.

docs.title: Render routes
docs.text:
Route Direction Args Description /render/enabled {0|1} inbound flag Toggle the render loop on or off; the GPU scheduler halts scene rendering while UI and adapter threads stay responsive /render/resolution {w} {h} inbound width, height Resize the render output surface (capability-gated render.custom-resolution) /render/fps {float} inbound target FPS Override the render FPS target

/render/enabled 0 is non-destructive: outbound audio, MIDI, and OSC state continue to publish, and shader pipelines remain warm so the restoration frame on /render/enabled 1 is within one frame budget. Useful for SMPTE-slaved setups, A/V calibration, and operator-triggered "hold current output" cues.

docs.title: Audio routes
docs.text:
Route Direction Args Description /audio/threshold {float} inbound and outbound clamped to [0, 1] Set or announce the audio noise-floor gate; updates syn_Threshold within one audio hop /audio/threshold/sample inbound (none) Sample the current 200 ms rolling RMS of syn_Level and set the threshold to that value; emits /audio/threshold {float} outbound on completion

Audio hops with RMS below the threshold publish zeroed syn_Level* and syn_*Hits family uniforms; the threshold is the operator's primary tool for rejecting room noise and HVAC bleed.

docs.title: Controls routes
docs.text: The /controls namespace is the runtime parameter-write surface used by external surfaces (TouchOSC, MIDI-to-OSC bridges, custom show runners). The canonical shape is /controls/{bank}/{control} followed by a typed value argument; the slice-2 router parses these into a canonical segment vector for the slice-3 dispatch surface that lands the typed-command translation. Author-side scenes declare their expected control bank in the scene script; the runtime rejects writes to unknown banks with a route-mismatch diagnostic.

docs.title: Plurality convention
docs.text:
The collection roots use the plural form (/scenes, /presets, /playlists, /favslots, /controls); action verbs and listing queries live under the collection root. Chromaticity V1 canonical form is plural-root throughout inbound and outbound emission. The singular reference-app forms (/scene/{name}, /preset/{name}, /playlist/next) are accepted as compat-syn-v1 aliases.

Authored from integrations/osc-adapter/src/routes.rs (slice-2 route-prefix taxonomy) and integrations/osc-adapter/src/defaults.rs (network defaults), against docs/adr/ADR-013-networking-defaults-and-security.md and the docs/08-io-integrations.md OSC sections. Clean-room per docs/29-cleanroom-legal-policy-baseline.md.
